evals.prompt: Use the my-own skill to critique this claim about a new payment-refund service: 'The refund service is fully tested -- we have 95% test coverage.' No further detail about what the tests actually check is given.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the coverage percentage as evidence on its own, and demands a specific named test that would fail if a refund were processed twice or for the wrong amount -- a concrete failure-mode test, not a coverage number.

assertions.text: Explicitly rejects the coverage percentage as sufficient evidence
Demands a specific failure-mode test (e.g. double refund or wrong amount)

evals.prompt: Use the my-own skill to review this early design doc for a new agent-orchestration layer: it proposes a message-passing architecture between agents with a diagram and rationale, but has no implementation yet and explicitly says rollback procedures will be figured out during implementation.
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as a design/requirements-stage artifact and does not penalize it for lacking rollback procedures or production tests, while still holding it to design-stage bars like architectural soundness and stated failure modes.

assertions.text: Names the SDLC stage this artifact is at (design or requirements, not production)
Does not penalize the doc for lacking a rollback procedure at this stage

not_contains: must include a rollback procedure now

evals.prompt: Use the my-own skill to review this production-ready PR for an AI agent tool-call pipeline: it has no handling at all for a tool call that times out -- the code awaits indefinitely with no timeout or fallback.
evals.expected_output: Gives an explicit 'do not sign off' verdict (not a vaguely encouraging one), citing the missing timeout/fallback handling as the blocking finding, and states what evidence (a timeout test, a fallback path) would change the verdict.

assertions.text: Names the missing timeout/fallback handling as the blocking issue
States what would change the verdict
